original_card.question: Can a decoder deliver the local paid mass in fewer, larger-rank children (block frame climbs instead of rank-1 to rank-3 steps)?
methods: Find one exact small decoding identity whose frame path climbs in blocks, and price its complete per-call profile.
Bound the best effective child rank achievable for one fixed support alphabet, including copies, frames and restoration.
original_card.acceptance_gate: A per-call local profile, with all copied information, frames and restoration counted, whose ceiling exceeds the selected word's by at least 5%; masked or overcomplete supports must change an assumption of the eight-term all-pairs bound. A scoped local result may be retained without a complete supplier. Expanding it into further construction rounds requires the family-level budget and obligation gate in research-family-status.md; an optimistic passing relaxation alone is not acceptance.

first_step.inspect: Read the selected word's per-call local profile, its packing ceiling and the lever table; run levers.py for the ideal budget of the lever you target.
first_step.scope: Positive control and planning budget only; this is not a new construction or full cold replay.

original_card.first_experiment: Before any synthesis, write the candidate per-call local profile (and centre charge / unpaid coordinates if changed) and screen it with ceiling.ceiling(); reject it if even the ideal ceiling does not beat the selected word's by your stated margin. Ideal budget: rank-16 delivery is 2.31x (levers.py).
original_card.bottleneck_link: Rank-1 children are about half of recursive cost; the selected word's effective child rank is about 3.9. Larger-rank delivery lowers recursive cost per unit of paid mass.
allowed_variations: One masked, overcomplete or block decoder family with exact labels and supports.
A scoped lower bound on effective rank for one alphabet.
If the coverage law, template or guard changes, derive an applicable fully charged replacement bound instead of applying the incumbent ceiling outside its scope.
scope_change_triggers: Repacking idle remainders of an unchanged word (covered by the packing ceiling).
Repeating the eight-term all-pairs search inside its proved scope.
Only changing helper terminal subspaces and monotone frames within the fixed scalar word, entrances and cleanup contract already covered by #1995/#2013.

Searching below C=40 in the #2017 Eisenstein binary scalar-rectangle or fixed-support block-linear additive pairing model; specify a changed premise instead. This bound does not cover every complex decoder.

Continuing a partial cost improvement while leaving the same unpriced consumer, restoration or central-readout obligation unresolved; refresh the family expansion decision first. Local product-retiming evidence has a narrow scope and is not a ban on changed graphs or contracts.

actual_scope: Can a decoder deliver the local paid mass in fewer, larger-rank children (block frame climbs instead of rank-1 to rank-3 steps)?
bottleneck_link: Rank-1 children are about half of the selected word's recursive cost (2,412 of 5,586 local mass; effective child rank about 3.9). Block-climb delivery in fewer, larger-rank children is the card's lever (ideal rank-16 budget 2.31x in levers.py). The complete per-call profile, with charged frame transports and restoration, decides whether any charged realization of that lever survives.
stop_rule: Stop at the smallest falsifying instance (the k=2 exact identity and its complete invoice), one bounded pivot to the PR 1605 threshold partitions and full reblock, and the recorded exact obstruction. Do not reprice the word's non-payload children, change the coverage law, or build a supplier.
evidence: RESULT.json: k=2 exact identity classification (matching payload pairs admit only coordinate-aligned child outputs; mixing with free decode additions exists only for shared-row/shared-column pairs and never reduces charged transports); dirty gather-slot restoration forces at least one paid rank-1 save per block; per-group charged-climb nets are strictly negative for every k in 2..51, every alpha >= 1 transports per group, and every a <= 1/99 (closed form: a block group pays only when k^a > alpha + 1, i.e. a > ln(1+alpha)/ln k >= ln2/ln51 > 0.1757); complete per-call screens at a* = 21/20 * 1690054109089/1e15 fail for every per-group charged realization (one shared rank-16 transport already fails, matching PR 1605), and the card's +5% ceiling gate is missed by every charged realization screened at the threshold partitions (best case with full idle credit reaches +4.5% over the baseline ceiling) while it stays open for call-level invoices within PR 1605's 10 added rank units; controls include an independent cost enclosure cross-check and PR 1605 threshold sign reproduction.
author: Aaron Wang
ai_assistance: Substantial opencode assistance in choosing the scope, deriving the identity classification and transport obstruction, implementing the exact arithmetic and verification, and writing the documentation; no model named; no independent human review.

open_questions.question: Do zero-charge co-frame climb groups exist among the selected word's actual 2,412 rank-one payload children?
open_questions.why_it_matters: Only alpha = 0 groups (both operand vectors already at the block frame, no restoration) clear the complete-profile gate; PR 1605's budget admits zero added work at its k = 363 threshold and up to 10 added rank units after full reblock, so co-frame coverage decides the whole lever.
open_questions.first_step: Read the pinned t16 canonical word's per-child operand frames, partition payload pairs whose two operand vectors already sit at one common rank-k frame, and price exactly those groups with zero charged transports.
open_questions.blocked_by: The per-child frame data lives in the pinned word archives (t16/global/base/providers/gauge44); extracting and classifying it is a separate data pass not attempted here.

open_questions.question: What complete profile results if a block climb also replaces the word's rank-2/rank-3 frame-step children (PR 1605 open question 2)?
open_questions.why_it_matters: Rank-one-only reblocking cannot reach a = 1/99; the frame-step children are the 'rank-1 to rank-3 steps' the card names, and subsuming them in one block climb is the only other mass-moving route.
open_questions.first_step: Declare the joint replacement contract (which step children each block group subsumes) and its coverage identity, then recompute the complete per-call profile before any synthesis.
open_questions.blocked_by: The coverage identity fixes paid mass at 72w + 64 per call; moving step mass requires a proved replacement identity, which this package does not supply.

entry.limits: Remote PR scope is open PRs including drafts. Closed work is searched through local READMEs, TASK metadata and ledger only. No code diffs or arbitrary package files are searched.
